exact_statement: Grimmett Question 2.2 asks whether a uniformly sampled n-step self-avoiding walk starting at the origin of the hexagonal lattice H converges weakly, after suitable rescaling as n tends to infinity, to an SLE_(8/3) random curve. The question leaves the exact scaling, curve geometry/stopping rule, and convergence topology unspecified.

primary_source.original_conjecture: Lawler, Schramm, Werner, On the scaling limit of planar self-avoiding walk, arXiv:math/0204277, https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0204277
primary_source.honeycomb_constant_and_local_identity: Duminil-Copin and Smirnov, The connective constant of the honeycomb lattice equals sqrt(2+sqrt2), arXiv:1007.0575, Theorem 1 and Lemma 1, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1007.0575#page=2

source_caveats: The all-length boundary-to-boundary critical-fugacity conjecture in arXiv:1206.2092 is related but is not the fixed-length origin-started P0003 question; transfer between ensembles is unproved here.
Grimmett Question 2.2 does not specify the rescaling, SLE geometry/stopping rule or curve topology; a proof must make these choices and justify them.
Conjecture 3.6 of arXiv:1206.2092 is a distinct unproved observable-limit conjecture.
The known connective constant and vertex identity alone do not prove a scaling limit.
